title: renewal-velocity-qbr-activation-checklist
summary: Compact facilitator playbook combining a focused QBR agenda, a short pre-meeting activation checklist, a scripted facilitation flow, and a simple renewal health rubric. Designed for 45-60m executive+operations QBRs where renewal visibility and next-step commitments matter more than long status dumps.
pre_meeting_checklist: Confirm primary attendees (exec sponsor, product owner, technical lead, procurement) — call out who must be present for renewal decision
Pull last quarter token usage and top-10 routes by spend (Console > Billing > Routes) — attach CSV
Export 2–3 representative prompts + responses to show typical latency and quality (redwood-console/exports) — anonymize customer data
Run renewal-health tool and snapshot current score (see linked Confluence), capture top 3 risk factors
Draft 3 prioritized agenda outcomes and proposed next steps (decide, approve, schedule) — include suggested owners
Prepare one slide showing SLA/latency trend and cost-per-1k-tokens baseline vs target
If applicable: prepare a quick canary-fallback demo (hosted vs dedicated) or diagram of routing policy
Send meeting brief and one-page pre-read 48 hours before meeting (attach prompts, metrics, ask for missing attendees)
Set calendar permissions and enable recording + shared notes doc
meeting_agenda: 0–5m: Quick context + 3 outcome goals (facilitator sets expectations)
5–15m: Usage snapshot and SLA highlights (ops owner) — show trends, anomalies, and cost signals
15–25m: Product impact stories (customer success + customer rep) — 1 positive, 1 pain point
25–35m: Risk and opportunities — renewal-health score review + top 3 risks and recommended mitigations
35–45m: Decision planning — renewal motion options (self-serve, committed, dedicated), tradeoffs and POA
45–55m: Commitments and owners — explicit actions, dates, and success criteria
55–60m: Quick closing pulse check + follow-up cadence (weekly checkpoints or escalation path)
facilitator_script:
Intro: Thanks everyone — quick housekeeping (timebox, notes, decision focus). State 3 desired outcomes: (1) shared view of health, (2) actionable renewal plan, (3) clear owners + dates.

Usage section: "Use plain language: here’s the last quarter in 90 seconds: cost up/down, latency SLOs hit/missed, and two routes that matter most. Ask ops: confirm any one-off events. If discrepancy appears, mark for post-meeting ops triage.

Impact stories: Invite the customer rep to share one win and one pain — keep to 3 minutes. If they hesitate, prompt: what changed for your users? what blocked your team?

Risk discussion: Read the top-3 risks from the health rubric aloud. For each risk: ask owner to state one mitigation they can commit to in 2 weeks. If no owner, propose an internal owner and note for follow-up.

Decision planning: Present the 3 renewal options (status quo, committed-reserved, upgrade-to-dedicated) with 1-slide pros/cons and cost impact. For shorter meetings, offer a recommendation and ask for thumbs-up/thumbs-down. If stakeholders need time, agree to a short follow-up vote within 7 calendar days.

Commitments: For each recorded action, confirm: owner, deliverable, due date, and where progress will be tracked (e.g., Confluence page or shared Trello). Read back aloud.

Close: Quick pulse — on a 1–5 confidence scale, how likely is the renewal motion to succeed? Capture answers in chat. Remind about next checkpoint and whom to escalate to if risks change.

Notes-to-self (facilitator): keep tempo, interrupt polite monologues, call out unresolved items and park them in 'parking lot' with owners, do not let technical deep-dives exceed 7 minutes — spin them into a follow-up tech session.
renewal_health_rubric: Score 8–10 (Green): Usage stable or growing, <2 SLA misses, single-point-of-failure mitigated, clear exec sponsor, NPS >= 8
Score 5–7 (Yellow): Usage fluctuating, 2–4 SLA incidents, moderate cost growth, sponsor engaged but not active, NPS 6–7
Score 0–4 (Red): Falling usage or concentration risk, >4 SLA incidents or a major outage in last 90 days, procurement/legal blockers, no exec sponsor, NPS <= 5
Quick signals to elevate: sudden 30% spend spike, new security/audit request, public outage in customer infra, legal/kickback clauses detected
post_meeting_followup_template: Subject line: QBR recap + agreed actions — [Customer] — [Date]
One-paragraph summary of decisions and renewal option chosen (or next decision date)
Bulleted action list: owner — deliverable — due date (linked where possible)
Link to recording, shared slide deck, exported prompts and metrics
Ask: Are there any missing stakeholders who should join the next checkpoint?
